prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, advancing frequency metrology to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I opened with IceCube (B059) first because I value detector-driven discoveries that open a new window. After reading the other seven ballots I move B013 to the top of my preferred configuration. It is the only candidate that six of seven ranking members place in the top three, and the support comes from members with different specialities: Kroll and Lindroth first, Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson second, myself third. The merit is concrete and instrument-based. Katori's magic-wavelength trapping removes the light-shift and motional errors, and Ye's strontium clocks brought systematic uncertainty to about 1e-18, with many laboratories now confirming each other in international comparisons. It enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches, and it underpins the discussion of redefining the second. This is a new measurement capability that has been independently reproduced and whose systematics are understood, which are the criteria I apply to my own field. The two-name credit is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the idea, and Ye pushed it to the accuracy and stability frontier.
statement.case_against: Ye already shared the 2005 prize for frequency-comb spectroscopy, so some members will see this as returning to the same laboratory family, and the contributions of other lattice-clock groups (SYRTE, PTB, NIST, Yb clocks) are real. Atomic and metrology physics is outside my own expertise, and I am relying on colleagues for the field-specific judgement. A further reservation is that the most broadly supported candidate is not necessarily the most scientifically important one. Opening support reflects clear attribution as much as scientific weight, and the Higgs experimental discovery arguably has greater weight but a structurally hard attribution problem. If the committee judges the Ye precedent to be disqualifying, B001 or B059 is my fallback.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks are a textbook case of a new measurement technique that moves the precision frontier by orders of magnitude, with timely recognition because the second may be redefined, and Katori and Ye are a clean pair.
responses.response: I agree and it is the main reason I now put B013 first. Reproduced 1e-18 comparisons between independent laboratories are the sort of calibration-and-systematics evidence I look for. I do not fully share your second choice. For NV centres (B009) I think the attribution is more contested than you suggest, since Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby and Walsworth all made decisive contributions, and I ranked it seventh.

responses.point: Eriksson puts magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B046) first as a case of experiment overturning theoretical expectation, but ranks B013 seventh and the Higgs eighth, citing field distance.
responses.response: I take the scientific case for moire matter seriously, and the prediction followed by experiment is attractive. But Mehlig, Lindroth and Johansson all point out that the superconducting mechanism is unresolved and the field is only about eight years past the 2018 experiments, and Olsson ranks it last. I see that as a maturity concern, not a defect of the physics, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald-Jarillo-Herrero credit also leaves out Yuan Cao and others. I would keep B046 for a later year. I also do not accept that the Higgs is low-ranked only because it is far from your field. Its experimental credit is hard, but the physics is unquestioned.

responses.point: The Event Horizon Telescope images (B016) are direct evidence of black-hole shadows, with Falcke and Doeleman as a defensible two-name configuration, and Danielsson ranks IceCube fifth.
responses.response: I ranked B016 fifth and share your view of its impact, but I cannot support omitting Zensus: his MPIfR group built the European mm-VLBI capability, and a two-name EHT prize from a collaboration of hundreds would be contested. The images also depend on reconstruction choices, and I would want more polarization and dynamics results first. On IceCube, where you ranked it fifth, I accept that source identification beyond the diffuse flux is still thin and that DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA predecessors complicate the credit.

responses.point: Circuit QED (B054) is the architecture behind superconducting processors, with Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf as theory plus two experimental leaders, and Johansson declares closeness to that area.
responses.response: I appreciate the declaration, and the physics is solid. My reservation is that the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is already close, and I would want the committee to be sure that the additional prize rests on distinct physics rather than on the platform success. No other member ranks it, so I treat it as a strong individual view that the rest of us should test, but I cannot yet place it above B013.

responses.point: Olsson ranks aberration-corrected electron optics (B015) first as an enabling instrument invention that is now routine and overdue, while ranking IceCube fourth and the Higgs third.
responses.response: As an instrument builder I am sympathetic: B015 is mature and has transformed materials physics, and I regard timing as late rather than premature. My concern is the credit, since Krivanek's STEM correction work is not in the list, and I would want the historical priority checked. I find the Higgs and clocks more compelling at present, but if the committee wanted a second part I would take your argument seriously.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards Ye's 2005 comb prize as a reason to prefer a different pair or candidate.

Whether a prize for the Higgs experimental discovery can be assigned to three individuals without arbitrary choice among Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee, and whether it should be given in the same year as a metrology prize.
Whether IceCube source identification has matured enough and how to weigh Halzen, Karle and Spiering against AMANDA/DUMAND/Baikal pioneers.
I cannot judge the finer attribution within lattice clocks (Lemonde, Ludlow, Derevianko) from outside atomic physics.
statement.conflict_note: I am a member of the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and work in astroparticle physics, which is adjacent to IceCube (B059) and the Event Horizon Telescope (B016); this may call for scrutiny of my opening first choice but is not a personal or institutional tie to the credited individuals as far as my profile shows. No specific conflict requiring recusal is apparent for B013 or B001.
